a.text: Once there was a red dragon of pride, who snubbed all companions, talking only to herself in the mirror from time to time.
Once, at Samhain, she was to host a grand banquet and her mirrored self was to help. But the two could not appear together before the guests, or the reflection would perish.
The reflection had no choice but to obey the dragon's will. She went and fetched the wakeman for the banquet. The wakeman rejected their invitation and told the reflection to desert.
Still, the reflection returned to the lair on her own, only to find the banquet had already begun. The reflection hurried to hide in darkness beyond the bonfire.
As the banquet went on, the guests somehow began to vanish, one by one. And the red dragon found and dragged her mirrored self out of the darkness, forcing the reflection to dance with her.
The two kept dancing, so relentlessly that the reflection could not feel her toes. She asked for a little rest, but the red dragon was never satisfied.

steps.text: Here, Loughshinny.
The book you wanted. The sequel to the Steam Knights adventures.
'Why', you ask?
Do I need a reason to do something for my beloved sister?
But, do you really need to read it?
Do you really need to read a book you have no interest in at all, but feel pressured by others our age to read?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I do want to read it.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Didn't you tell Father you didn't want anyone asking you why a Victorian wouldn't enjoy stories about the Steam Knights?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This book... did Dad ask you to buy it for me?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Why do you ask?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Because... how did you know?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You're backing away from me, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I don't want you to be scared of me like everyone else.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, I...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If me knowing what you told Father is so scary, how about we dance together to calm you down? Hm?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: A... dance? Really?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Why not?
With those words, Eblana gracefully extends a hand towards her sister.
But in Loughshinny's memories, even when her parents put on their favorite music, even when Father shook his head to the melody, even when Mother tapped her fingers to the beat...
Her sister would only sit perfectly still while bearing an icy smile.
She had never moved her body to any tune. Not even once.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Once you can keep up with me, you'll no longer have to worry about any book, request, or even friends our age.
The unopened knight novel falls to the ground, and the pleasant new book smell is now drowned by muddy water.
She was still young then. She never imagined that achieving her desires could feel so heavy and bitter. She only remembers stumbling, turning away, ignoring what was reaching out to her...
A soft and cold hand.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Loughshinny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The crowd is gone. You need no longer hide your identity.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Do you still think of them as alive, even now?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I only know that every Taran's heart burns with a similar flame. And that ever since our ancestors first bent the knee to the Victorians, that flame has never gone out.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: That goes for all the townsfolk, as well as those who followed me back here. They all have the same fire, except that theirs has never been tainted by the shade of death.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: What a wonderful analogy, Loughshinny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Then let me ask you again: what will you do?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Dye these flames in your own hue? I imagine you must have tried already.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: No matter who they are, once tainted by death, your flames can only render them into ash.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: So I have a proposal, Loughshinny. Kill me.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: And everyone in the city as well?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: If it bothers you how this will be recorded in history, then you can just say that I killed them, and that you merely laid them to rest.

spans.text: If it bothers you how this will be recorded in history, then you can just say that
killed them, and that you merely laid them to rest.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The people of Na Saoirsí are still alive.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Even if what animates their bodies is not life, but death?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: If they were truly devoid of even the faintest spark of life, they would have long since become one of those hollow, shambling corpses you have wandering about.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Oh, they will. Eventually.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No, they won't.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I'd rather see the purple flames in them as a plague, one instigated by you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: And you plan to find a cure for it?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I want to cure you of it as well, Eblana.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: How wonderful.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Wonderful?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Yes. That's absolutely wonderful.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Did you not notice?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You aren't trying to run from me anymore. You're trying to cure me, of all things.

spans.text: You aren't trying to run from me anymore. You're trying to

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Come, dance with me, Loughshinny. The same dance I've always invited you to, the one you always ran from.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What... did you say?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I asked you to dance with me.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But before the final bar, be sure to pierce my heart with your spear. This plague is lethal, and there is no cure. I do not question your resolve, but your efforts will be in vain.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You've run from your fate long enough... From Na Saoirsí's fate, and ours too.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: It is not yet Samhain, but the boundary between life and death is more ambiguous than it has been in all of Taran history.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Do you truly wish for Tara to become a kingdom of death?
Loughshinny subconsciously turns her head away.
The fierce purple flames still rage in the skeleton the hero dragged all the way here. Culann, now taken over by purple flames, briefly stands up before sinking back down to kneel.
She cannot bear another look at him, so she turns her gaze back to her sister's eyes—and the hand she's been offered for so many years.

It is unclear if it is her imagination or a side effect of the purple flames depriving everything they touch of vitality, but the hand before her seems so pale and bloodless compared to the one in her memories.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We speak of a city and the lives of countless people, Eblana. You cannot sum this up as a matter as simple as 'fate'.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Are you finished? I believe we've spent enough time talking past each other.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Eblana!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Oh, but feel free to continue. If you so desire, I shall wait here for as long as you need me to.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But do try not to take too long. You can afford to wait, yet that may not be true for others.

spans.text: But do try not to take
long. You can afford to wait, yet that may not be true for others.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: (Breathes deeply) You're right. You can afford to wait, but that may not be true for others.

spans.text: can afford to wait, but that may not be true for others.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Alright. I'll dance your dance. Until one of us falls and can dance no more.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But I will not follow your lead. Absolutely not.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: As you please.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Though you seem to have misunderstood something, my dear Loughshinny.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The one who cannot afford to wait is standing before you now.
'Cannot afford to wait'?
Loughshinny scrutinizes her sister's face as she suddenly realizes something entirely unrelated to their conversation.
The offered hand is indeed pale, and it is not just her imagination.

Purple flames seem to weave together into an omnipresent cloak, giving Eblana her beautiful yet terrifying appearance. Yet they also fail to conceal the malady which seems to consume her beneath her pale white skin.
She shouldn't be like this. She was never like this before.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Eblana, are you...

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Are you... alright, Sister?
A smile spreads across Eblana's face. The same old ice-cold smile is always found there.
This time, it seems to bear some warmth, but this only highlights her conspicuous paleness.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I appreciate your concern. Really, I do.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: After all those apathetic partings and painful reunions, to only now hear you asking if I'm well... It has truly been so long.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Incidentally, I really do want a dance with you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...I will, once I find a way to heal you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Very well. Then I shall await you here.
Eblana strides towards the citadel, her footsteps so faint that they seem almost frail.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Hoo... Red dragon! Nemos!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: There was no one at the gates when I got back! I thought something must've happened! What's going on in the square—

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Red dragon... what's that...?
Loughshinny is holding a small box in her arms. The dim night lights seem to make it harder than usual to see.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I couldn't save Culann. I...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This was the only way for him to rest in peace. So he'd no longer have to suffer from the flames in the square.
The nomad is silent for a long time, until she finds a stone on the ground.
She hurls it with all her strength towards the citadel.
But the darkness of the night swallows it up, and it fails to even make a sound.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It's already past curfew. Nemos, Brigid, let's just—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No.
Nemos reaches out to the wooden box, as if trying to brush nonexistent dust off the lid.
She suddenly recalls being rejected by her own people a few days ago, and the superfluous words she heard then.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: The wakemen do not stand with the living, nor do we require their reverence. Until, of course, they are dead.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: That is the tradition Dublinn should be honoring.

spans.text: is the tradition Dublinn should be honoring.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Still, I'm grateful you were at least willing to give me this whistle... I'll be going now.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Wait, Nemos. You knew well that Samhain approaches and the wakemen would be lacking sacred instruments. Yet you still came.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Did the Dublinners force you to?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No, I came here of my own—

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: Nemos, you haven't changed one bit.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: You wait, mediate, and reconcile... Are you also like this in Na Saoirsí? Do you also serve the Red Dragon like this?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I just... don't want to see a situation that could be improved deteriorate any further. Or people who could have cooperated fighting each other.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: If conflict is inevitable, you will only ever sink deeper into the mire.

steps.name: Solemn Wakewoman
steps.text: The city has tainted you with its darkness, Nemos.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: So, The Leader—the Red Dragon—

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Eblana will never give Na Saoirsí true life? Is that right, Loughshinny?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: She said she couldn't. She... actually doesn't like to lie, unless there are other circumstances...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: She's The Leader of Tara, the one and only Red Dragon, what could possibly be tying her hands?!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What's wrong, Nemos? You seem... different...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I get it. I finally get it, Your Highness Loughshinny.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: It seems that that fire can in fact infect the living.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Nemos?!

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: The people I once depended on turned out to be a swarm of selfish parasites.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: The Leader I once believed in turned out to be an evil dragon who doesn't care if anyone else lives or dies.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: The people I once put my life on the line to protect... became the reason my closest friend died.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I can't even imagine what they would have done to him if that wicked dragon hadn't lit him up with her flames.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Culann was right to ask what we would do once Samhain is over. What should I do?

spans.text: Culann was right to ask what we would do once Samhain is over. What

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Other than revenge, there's nothing left for me either.
As she utters these words, Loughshinny sees a flame ignite within the final Na Saoirsían left untainted by the purple fire.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Your Highness, will you regard me the same as the rest of the residents—a servant of Eblana?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: No. This deadly disease... It has ultimately infected even the last person in the city.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: If so, Your Highness, then I swear to you that I will aid you in this dance that's been forced on you. Until the very end...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Until the wicked dragon falls.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...I have heard your vow.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Now, I must leave the city for a while. Come with me, Nemos.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: To the wakemen?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Mhm. I have no hope of curing the flame here, so I thought we should seek aid from anyone who might be able to help.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No, I can't go with you. I have no right to be there anymore.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'll stay in the city. As long as the Red Dragon doesn't realize what's going on and tear me apart... I'll try my best to keep the situation from deteriorating.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Though, I'd appreciate it if you could return this whistle for me.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: And... Culann too. Please give him a proper funeral.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: A proper funeral requires eulogies from friends and family, so... I'll write one. Could you read it for me there?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Here. It's done.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I'll go with Reed. The Dark Woods aren't lettin' anyone in or out, but it should be smoother with us two.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: No, Brigid. You should stay too. I need your help.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Reed?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I'll be fine by myself.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: That works, but... Nemos, you're so different now.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: ...I guess this is what vengeance does to a person.
